text: Many quorum-sensing-controlled behaviors (secreted digestive enzymes, biofilm matrix, secreted toxins) are treated as 'public goods.' Why does this framing predict an evolutionary vulnerability for quorum-sensing populations?
choices: Public goods cannot diffuse away from the cell that produces them
Producing public goods is metabolically free, so overproduction wastes nothing
Non-producing 'cheater' cells can exploit the shared resource without paying its production cost, gaining a relative fitness advantage
Public goods are always toxic to the bacteria that produce them
explanation: A public good is individually costly but collectively beneficial, so 'cheaters' that stop producing it while still consuming it gain a relative fitness advantage, threatening cooperation (the framework developed in the social-evolution work of Stuart West and colleagues). Option 0 is false, since diffusibility is exactly what makes the good shareable; option 1 is false, because production is costly (the crux of the problem); and option 3 is false, as such goods are not generally toxic to producers.
